newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Court says concurrent pensions start on first valid date.
newsitem.headline: Court says concurrent pensions start on first valid date.

text.p: The European Court of Justice ruled on Thursday pension regulations allowing concurrent awards from different member states are not negated even if the beneficiary's first claim is not filed in the resident state.
The court said the reference date for granting pension benefits is the first date a valid claim is awarded from any member state.

"Any claim...which should have been submitted...within a specified period to an authority...shall be admissible if it is submitted to a corresponding authority....," the court said, quoting Council regulation 1408/71.
The court said the reason Community regulations direct claimants to file first with their place of residence is to promote administrative simplification, not to penalize them.

Michel Picard received pension benefits from France, but was rejected by the Belgians. Eventually the Belgians agreed to give benefits, but argued the start date was based on when Picard applied in Belgium, not in France.
The court has now said Belgium must respect Picard's filing date in France.
(Court translation into English. Original language of the case: French)

"Social security for migrant workers - Old age and death insurance - Benefits - Concurrent award of pensions under the legislation of two member states - Automatic award upon submission of a claim to the competent institution of one of the member states - Claim to be made to the institution of the member state of residence in order to obtain award of both pensions concurrently"
Reference from the Cour du Travail, Liege, Belgium for a preliminary ruling in the case pending between
Institut National d'Assurance Sociales pour Travailleurs Independants (Inasti)

on the interpretation of article 36 of regulation (EEC) No 574/72 of the Council of 21 March 1972 laying down the procedure for implementing regulaiton (EEC) No 1408/71 on the application of social security schemes to employed persons, self-employed persons and members of their families moving within the Community, as amended and updated by Council regulation (EEC) No 2001/83 of 2 June 1983 (OJ 1983 L 230, p. 86)

Article 36(4) regulation (EEC) No 574/72 of the Council of 21 March 1972 laying down the procedure for implementing regulation (EEC) No 1408/71 on the application of social security schemes to employed persons, self-employed persons and members of their families moving within the Community, as amended and updated by Council regulation (EEC) No 2001/83 of 2 June 1983, which provides for the concurrent award of benefits when a claim for benefits is submitted to an institution of a member state, lays down an independent procedural rule which applies regardless of whether the provisions of article 36(1) to (3) have been complied with.
